sections.what_happened: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- NBC, two US officials, Nov 6] Some administration and defence officials told Trump five days before Tuesday's midterm elections that if he restarts major combat operations against Iran, he should do so before the swearing-in of the new Congress in January -- roughly an eight-week window. Democrats' takeover of both houses reinforced the assessment; a new Congress could hamper operations through investigations, budget cuts and legislative action. Trump received an updated briefing on Thursday Nov 5 (Hegseth + Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine); no final decision; Pentagon declined to comment; White House official: Trump has 'all options available at any time.' [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- Washington Post / Ignatius, knowledgeable US official, Nov 7] Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, with Trump's blessing, reached out to China to use its influence with Tehran to end the Iran war after the Republican midterm rout, which Trump and Vance publicly attribute to the war; China has conveyed the message to Tehran. VP Vance leads diplomatic efforts (letter to Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei last month via Qatari intermediaries). Trump asked Xi for help on Iran in September; Xi told him privately Iran should never have a nuclear weapon; the issue is expected up again when Trump and Xi meet in Shenzhen on November 18. China said its Middle East envoy would visit Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia this month on shuttle diplomacy. [CONTEXT] Same story family as the WSJ advisers split recorded at 1100-01 (Hegseth/Cooper vs Vance/Witkoff) and the Axios three-camp reporting (1500-03(d)); Qatar bridge-deal mediation recorded at 1200-04.
sections.what_verified: Washington Post (T2) is the origin of the Bessent-China report; Times of Israel (T3) and Times of India (T3) carry both reports. NBC is NOT in the source registry -- attribution only, does not count toward corroboration.
sections.what_disputed: Neither Washington nor Beijing has commented publicly on the China request (Thursday Times). Trump has not made a final decision on resuming operations. The Pentagon declined to comment on the NBC report. The eight-week window is the advisers' political calculation, not an announced strike date (Clash Report). A separate dailyimroz/TASS claim that Fox News reported a Nov 9 resumption date is UNVERIFIED -- see triage 1700-07(b); do not present Nov 9 as a date.
sections.why_matters: Eight weeks. That's the clock Trump's own advisers put on the Iran war -- and now his Treasury chief is asking China to end it. Strike or deal: the decision is coming.

totw_analysis: Our read: Eight weeks. That's the clock Trump's own advisers put on the Iran war -- and now his Treasury chief is asking China to end it. Strike or deal: the decision is coming. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Strike before January or cut a deal -- did the midterm defeat force Trump to end the war, or to restart it?
